rows.note: The original open turn resumes after lease expiry; the first model body has not run.
The provider body returned, but its attempt result did not commit. Recovery records outcome_unknown without replaying the body.

SIGKILL follows the exact executor fiber-exit/action-commit barrier and an independently observed single external effect. A fresh process reconciles the open intent as outcome_unknown without reexecution; the receipt-present variant resumes from its committed boundary. This tests process crash, not power loss.
Executor recovery preserves the already committed logical model result and does not append or execute it again. This is not a claim about replaying the whole chat loop.
Both bodies returned; only the first positional result committed. That result survives, while the second settles outcome_unknown without replay.

A committed retry.scheduled alarm (kind at) survives the crash; boot recovery consumes (cancels) the schedule via the single alarm owner and wakes the session, and the resumed turn completes the attempt exactly once.
The summary, successor projection and accounting committed in one ledger transaction before any publication. Recovery folds to the committed boundary without resummarizing.
The atomic inbox admission committed, but no turn opened. A new handle consumes that same inbox message once. No partial SQLite transaction is simulated.
The source turn and reply obligation committed. Recovery dispatches the same pending reply and settles its delivery without executing the source runner again.

Two processes stop before the model: the first leaves the original turn open, the second commits a resume and stops at runner entry. Final wake preserves turnId, records resumeCount 2, executes one model call and settles once. Unlike the rearmed target, there is no separately durable recovery-dispatch/RPC identity; the current mechanism resumes the same turn.

Cut after the compaction result commit and before caller/event publication. Executor recovery appends nothing and history folds to the committed summary projection without resummarizing. This nearest current cut does not claim atomic successor, parent closure, accounting or handoff publication.

Cut at the empty release-lease commit after the ack succeeds. Wake dispatches zero deliveries and preserves delivered state; the expired lease is reacquirable and explicit cleanup releases it, with revision stable on another wake. Idle wake does not itself clean up the old lease.

SIGKILL after a counted external stand-in send and destination SQLite admission, before returning the receipt. A fresh process reconciles the receiver's durable receipt without dispatch, consumes one destination prompt and preserves one source terminal; the non-deduplicating external counter stays one. This proves ledger-visible sent receipts, not remote adapters without a durable receipt.

SIGKILL at dispatcher entry after the outbound open row, before any platform-side effect. A fresh process sends once and a second wake sends nothing. No durable attempt marker or not_sent reconciliation exists: the current outbound contract only admits pending/delivered. Target proof remains blocked, not claimed by the rearmed class.

External stand-in appends messageId to a non-deduplicating side file, then SIGKILL before any receiver receipt. Fresh-process recovery sends again; external count is two. The lost/outcome_unknown target is blocked: the ledger's strict outbound projection admits only pending/delivered, with no attempt/reconciliation/unknown state. No alternate agent-owned state store was introduced.

The summarizer admits a foreign tail prompt before returning; cut follows the compaction result commit. Recovery preserves the summary projection unchanged and exactly one pending tail inbox row. This current cut demonstrates inbox preservation, not a durable watermark/ceiling or successor handoff.

SIGKILL after flood refusal propagates; a fresh process retries immediately and then sends nothing on repeated wake. No persisted outbound notBefore/deadline or atomic outbound+alarm transition exists. Residual rearm and zero attempts before the deadline remain blocked; this is only the honest current rearmed class.

SIGKILL immediately after alarm.fire commits its occurrence and inbox prompt for a hibernated session, before a doorbell. A fresh process reopens the same SQLite database and wakes once; one runner consumes the original prompt, the alarm stays fired with one occurrence, and another wake does not execute. TestClock supplies logical time; the ledger mints the occurrence identity.
Successor fence rejects the stale result atomically; separately, executor recovery settles the old attempt outcome_unknown without replay. This does not prove shared-lineage alias rejection.
B6 pre-boundary fault variant: summary returned but no boundary/result committed; recovery cannot publish the uncommitted summary.
R1 crosswalk to imported draft ID: exact 256-action threshold commits its checkpoint before owner exit; fresh-process bounded hydration equals the full oracle.
R2: selected context restoration result and fold checkpoint commit before the executor releases publication; exact projection survives fresh-process hydration.

R3 crosswalk to imported draft ID: SIGKILL after a valid checkpoint, then deliberate seed-hash corruption with intact action chain; fresh wake refuses FoldCheckpointIntegrityError with zero runner entries and zero range reads. Not a power-loss simulation.
R4: a post-checkpoint snapshot updates the existing message identity; fresh bounded state and projection equal the complete action-tree oracle exactly.
R5: checkpoint retains the entered tool intent before its terminal; recovery retains the captured identity and records outcome_unknown without re-entering the tool.

R6 fault cell: after killing an open generation-one turn with generation two selected, the fresh executable provider omits the captured generation; GenerationUnavailable refuses before runner entry, never substituting generation two.
